correctness.rationale: A generic section vertex is precisely a crossed polytope edge. At the octahedron endpoint, 3 positive and 3 negative vertices have 3 antipodal nonedges, giving 6 crossings. At the cuboctahedron, 24 edges partition into 6 squares, whose sign transitions contribute 0+4+4=8 for each generic sorted normal. For every t<2 or t>2, the diagonal plane gives a stable hexagon, while a nearly coordinate-plane section gives a stable octagon for 1<t<2 or stable square for 2<t<=3. Nonempty normal neighborhoods have positive Haar measure. Independent exact rational facet-intersection computations corroborate finite examples; no finite test is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: This closes a naturally formulated full-interval structural classification: the octahedron and isolated cuboctahedron are precisely the almost-sure constant-section-complexity bodies in the standard cube–octahedron interpolation. It singles out a nonendpoint rigidity not forced by the generic count at cube/octahedron, with explicit geometric witnesses for all other parameters. It is neither a single unmotivated numerical evaluation nor merely renaming the known packing or illumination results.
